reviewNotes: Do not treat several regional networks as proof of one continuous intercontinental north-south route. Object provenance is not proof of direct unmediated trade, migration or language spread.

Parrot species identification, feather provenance, live-animal transport inference and modeled corridors are different claims. Least-cost paths are hypotheses, not excavated roads; animal DNA is not human ancestry.
Preserve Indigenous trader-diplomat oral-tradition interpretation with its evidence type; Bloch 2018 is not automatically a primary sourcing study for every commodity listed.
Screen Seijas 2019 for book-review status; PNAS In This Issue is a summary requiring underlying research. Erratum is not an independent study; Chard publication year requires checking.
Anatolia/Levant/Mesopotamia and Asian transport studies are comparative context, not direct evidence of ancient American trade.
Experimental reed-boat voyage does not establish prehistoric transatlantic contact. Preserve the claim as an unverified lead, not a mapped route.
Baño Nuevo 1 narrative and table give different temporal scopes; recover specimen-specific ages rather than assuming continuous 11000-year exchange.
Consensus percentage is search-result metadata, not measured scholarly agreement or a probability. Figure captions are retained; no actual figures or reuse license were supplied.
